dataAsOf: FY 2025-26 (plant data as per CEA, MoP, company annual reports)
dataSource: CEA installed capacity reports, NTPC/Adani/Tata Power/Vedanta annual reports, MoP press releases
note: Unit configurations (e.g. 4×660 MW) reflect actual turbine-generator sets at each plant. Equipment manufacturer data from CEA/BHEL/company filings. Capacity figures rounded to nearest MW.

turbineGeneratorOEMs.name: Bharat Heavy Electricals Ltd
turbineGeneratorOEMs.note: Dominant domestic OEM; manufactures 210/250/500/660/800 MW steam turbines, generators, boilers under license from GE/Siemens/Alstom. ~70% of India's thermal fleet.

turbineGeneratorOEMs.name: GE Power (Baker Hughes)
turbineGeneratorOEMs.note: Supplies 660/800 MW supercritical turbines. BHEL manufactures under GE license for 660 MW units.

turbineGeneratorOEMs.name: Siemens Energy
turbineGeneratorOEMs.note: 660/800 MW supercritical sets. BHEL-Siemens joint supply for several NTPC projects.

turbineGeneratorOEMs.name: Alstom (now GE Vernova)
turbineGeneratorOEMs.note: 500/660 MW turbines. Supplied turbines to Tata Power, Adani Power units.

turbineGeneratorOEMs.name: Doosan Heavy Industries
turbineGeneratorOEMs.note: 660/870 MW supercritical turbines for private developers. Significant presence in Adani/Sterlite fleet.

turbineGeneratorOEMs.name: Harbin Electric (HEC)
turbineGeneratorOEMs.note: 600/660 MW turbines. Used in some private sector projects pre-2020.

turbineGeneratorOEMs.name: Toshiba Energy Systems
turbineGeneratorOEMs.note: Supplied generators for select NTPC and private developer units.

turbineGeneratorOEMs.name: L&T-MHI Turbine Generators
turbineGeneratorOEMs.note: Joint venture: Larsen & Toubro + Mitsubishi Hitachi Power. Manufactures 660/800 MW steam turbine generators in India.

boilerOEMs.name: BHEL (Boiler Division)
boilerOEMs.note: Manufactures pulverised coal boilers for 210/250/500/660/800 MW units. ~65% market share.

boilerOEMs.name: Cethar Limited
boilerOEMs.note: CFBC and AFBC boilers for smaller 30–300 MW units. Listed on BSE.

boilerOEMs.name: Thermax Ltd
boilerOEMs.note: Boilers for smaller industrial and sub-100 MW units.

boilerOEMs.name: Dongfang Electric (DEC)
boilerOEMs.note: Supercritical boilers for 660 MW units in some private sector projects.

boilerOEMs.name: Mitsui Babcock / Hitachi Zosen
boilerOEMs.note: High-pressure boilers for select older NTPC units.

thermalOperators.name: NTPC Limited
thermalOperators.source: NTPC Annual Report FY2025-26; CEA installed capacity Mar 2026
thermalOperators.notes: India's largest power utility. ~25% of India's total installed capacity. Operates 23 coal/gas stations.

units.note: India's first supercritical units

plants.note: Low PLF due to gas shortage

plants.plantName: NTPC Kudgi Super Thermal Power Station

units.note: BHEL 800 MW supercritical — largest domestic units. BHEL-GE collaboration.

thermalOperators.name: Adani Power Limited
thermalOperators.source: Adani Power Annual Report FY2025-26; BSE filings
thermalOperators.notes: India's largest private thermal power producer. Fleet of supercritical and ultra-supercritical plants.

units.note: Imported coal (Indonesia). Coastal location — cyclone/flood exposed.

thermalOperators.name: Tata Power Company Limited
thermalOperators.notes: Oldest private power utility in India. Iconic Trombay plant in Mumbai. Also operates Coastal Gujarat.

plants.note: Supplies power to Mumbai. Aging fleet — partial decommissioning expected.

units.note: Largest supercritical units in India at time of commissioning. Coastal — exposed to cyclone & flood.

thermalOperators.name: Vedanta / TSPL (Talwandi Sabo)
thermalOperators.source: Vedanta Annual Report FY25; Punjab Energy Sector data
thermalOperators.notes: Talwandi Sabo Power (TSPL) in Punjab + Jharsuguda plant in Odisha. Both supercritical.

units.note: Captive plant for aluminium smelter. April 2025 explosion — 25 fatalities.

thermalOperators.name: JSW Energy (Thermal Fleet)
thermalOperators.notes: Thermal fleet includes Vijayanagar (Karnataka) and Ratnagiri (Maharashtra). Transitioning to RE.

units.note: Very low PLF due to domestic gas shortage.

thermalOperators.name: Sembcorp Energy India (Thermal)
thermalOperators.notes: TPCIL (Thermal Powertech Corporation India) — 2×660 MW supercritical at Krishnapatnam, AP.

units.note: Coastal Andhra Pradesh — cyclone exposed. Imported coal from Indonesia/Australia.

thermalOperators.name: CESC Limited
thermalOperators.notes: Distribution utility for Kolkata. Owns and operates coal plants supplying Kolkata.

thermalOperators.name: Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC)
thermalOperators.source: DVC Annual Report FY25; CEA data
thermalOperators.notes: Joint venture between Govt of India, West Bengal and Jharkhand. Coal basket region.

thermalOperators.name: MAHAGENCO (Maharashtra State Power Generation Co.)
thermalOperators.notes: Maharashtra's state genco. Largest state-owned thermal utility. Coal fleet across 7 stations. Also has hydro and solar.

units.note: Partially retired due to environmental compliance issues.

thermalOperators.name: TANGEDCO (Tamil Nadu Generation & Distribution Corp.)
thermalOperators.source: TANGEDCO website; CEA installed capacity data
thermalOperators.notes: Tamil Nadu's state genco. Fleet of older subcritical coal plants. Tuticorin is the flagship.

units.note: Coastal plant — cyclone exposed. Oldest TANGEDCO thermal.

thermalOperators.name: APGENCO (Andhra Pradesh Power Generation Corp.)
thermalOperators.notes: Andhra Pradesh state genco. Dr. Narla Tata Rao TPS (Vijayawada) is the flagship.

thermalOperators.name: TSGENCO (Telangana State Power Generation Corp.)
thermalOperators.notes: Telangana state genco (carved from APGENCO 2014). Operates Kothagudem, Ramagundam-B, Bhadradri.

units.note: Oldest state genco plant in operation.

thermalOperators.name: GSECL (Gujarat State Electricity Corporation Ltd)
thermalOperators.notes: Gujarat state genco. Wanakbori, Ukai, Gandhinagar, Dhuvaran stations. Mix of coal, gas, lignite.

thermalOperators.name: RRVUNL (Rajasthan Rajya Vidyut Utpadan Nigam Ltd)
thermalOperators.notes: Rajasthan state genco. Suratgarh and Kota stations. Also operates lignite plants at Barsingsar.

thermalOperators.name: UPRVUNL (UP Rajya Vidyut Utpadan Nigam Ltd)
thermalOperators.notes: Uttar Pradesh state genco. Obra, Anpara, Parichha, Harduaganj stations.

units.note: One of India's oldest thermal stations.

thermalOperators.name: WBPDCL (West Bengal Power Development Corp. Ltd)
thermalOperators.notes: West Bengal state genco. Bakreswar and Sagardighi stations are the largest.

thermalOperators.name: MPPGCL (MP Power Generating Company Ltd)
thermalOperators.notes: Madhya Pradesh state genco. Sanjay Gandhi TPS (Birsinghpur) and Satpura are key stations.

thermalOperators.name: CSPGCL (Chhattisgarh State Power Generation Co.)
thermalOperators.notes: Chhattisgarh state genco. Coal-rich state. Hasdeo Bango, Korba-East stations.

thermalOperators.name: Jindal Steel & Power Ltd (JPL — Power Division)
thermalOperators.notes: Captive + merchant power from coal plants near steel operations. Tamnar (CG) is the largest.

thermalOperators.name: Torrent Power Limited
thermalOperators.notes: Integrated utility (generation + distribution in Ahmedabad/Surat/Bhiwandi). Gas + coal fleet.

plants.note: Low PLF due to domestic gas shortage.

thermalOperators.name: NLC India Limited
thermalOperators.source: NLC India Annual Report FY25; CEA
thermalOperators.notes: Lignite mining + power. Oldest lignite-based power utility. Also expanding into solar. Neyveli complex is India's lignite capital.

thermalOperators.name: Reliance Power Limited
thermalOperators.source: Reliance Power Annual Report FY25; BSE filings
thermalOperators.notes: Anil Ambani group. Sasan UMPP is the flagship — India's largest private coal plant. Also Krishnapatnam and Rosa.

units.note: India's largest single-location coal plant. Captive coal mine (low fuel cost). Sasan won on lowest tariff — ₹1.19/kWh.

thermalOperators.name: PSPCL (Punjab State Power Corp. Ltd)
thermalOperators.notes: Punjab's combined genco+discom. Ropar and Lehra Mohabbat stations.

thermalOperators.name: MB Power (Madhya Pradesh) Ltd
thermalOperators.notes: Japanese-consortium owned supercritical plant at Anuppur (MP). Mitsui & Co. is majority stakeholder. Supplies power to MP DISCOMs under long-term PPA.

thermalOperators.name: Lalitpur Power Generation Company Ltd
thermalOperators.notes: Bajaj Group's power generation arm. Supercritical plant at Lalitpur (UP). Long-term PPA with UP DISCOMs.

thermalOperators.name: Jindal India Power Ltd (JIPL, formerly Jindal India Thermal Power Ltd)
thermalOperators.source: Jindal India Power Ltd (company website); CEA
thermalOperators.notes: Coal-based thermal plant at Derang Village, Angul, Odisha. 1,200 MW (2×600 MW) operating since 2015. BTG package by BHEL; coal from Talcher/MCL; water from Brahmani River (upstream of Samal Barrage). Proposed Angul-II expansion: 1,320 MW (2×660 MW).

units.note: Coal from Talcher coalfields / Mahanadi Coalfields Ltd (MCL); water from Brahmani River upstream of Samal Barrage.

thermalOperators.name: DB Power Ltd (Diligent Power)
thermalOperators.notes: Supercritical plant in Chhattisgarh. Formerly associated with Moser Baer group, now under Diligent Group management after restructuring.

thermalOperators.name: SKS Power Generation (Chhattisgarh) Ltd
thermalOperators.notes: Medium-sized thermal IPP in coal-rich Chhattisgarh.

thermalOperators.name: RattanIndia Power Ltd
thermalOperators.notes: Formerly Indiabulls Power. Two large supercritical plants — Amravati (MH) and Nasik (MH). Debt-stressed but operational.

thermalOperators.name: Coastal Energen Pvt Ltd (formerly IL&FS Tamil Nadu Power)
thermalOperators.notes: Coastal imported-coal plant at Tuticorin, TN. Originally IL&FS project, acquired by new investors after IL&FS collapse (2018). Coastal location = cyclone exposed.

units.note: Imported coal from Indonesia. Coastal — cyclone & flood exposed.

thermalOperators.name: GMR Energy Ltd (Thermal Division)
thermalOperators.notes: GMR Group's power division. Plants in AP and CG. Partially divesting thermal to focus on airports/urban infra. EMCO Warora plant sold to Adani.

thermalOperators.name: Lanco Amarkantak Power Ltd (now under NCLT)
thermalOperators.notes: Former Lanco Group asset. Under NCLT resolution (debt-stressed). 2×660 MW supercritical at Korba (CG). May be acquired by Adani/other. Currently operational under interim management.

units.note: Under NCLT resolution. May change ownership.

thermalOperators.name: Essar Power (Mahan / Salaya)
thermalOperators.listed: Unlisted (Essar Group — partially divested to Adani)
thermalOperators.source: Essar Group; CEA; Adani acquisition data
thermalOperators.notes: Essar Group's power plants — Mahan (MP) sold to Adani, Salaya (Gujarat) under Essar. Partially divested portfolio.

units.note: Coastal Gujarat — imported coal. Cyclone exposed.

thermalOperators.name: Bajaj Energy Ltd (Meja Urja Nigam JV)
thermalOperators.source: Bajaj Energy IPO documents; BSE filings
thermalOperators.notes: Bajaj Group listed power entity. Portfolio includes Lalitpur (3×660 MW via subsidiary) and Meja STPS JV with NTPC. Supplies power to UP grid.

units.note: 50:50 JV with NTPC. NTPC operates.

thermalOperators.name: KSK Energy Ventures (under NCLT)
thermalOperators.notes: KSK Mahanadi Power project (CG). One of India's largest stressed thermal assets. Under NCLT resolution. 1800 MW operational but ownership under dispute.

units.note: Under NCLT resolution. Operational but stressed asset.

thermalOperators.name: Athena Chhattisgarh Power Ltd
thermalOperators.notes: 1200 MW plant in Chhattisgarh. One of several medium-sized private IPPs in coal-rich CG corridor.

thermalOperators.name: IL&FS Energy (various plants — under resolution)
thermalOperators.notes: Multiple thermal projects under IL&FS group resolution. Some sold (Coastal Energen to new owners), others pending. IL&FS collapse (2018) was India's largest corporate distress event.

hydroOperators.name: NHPC Limited
hydroOperators.notes: India's largest hydro power utility. Operates 25 hydroelectric projects. Expansion into solar.

units.note: Long-delayed project. Francis turbines by BHEL.

hydroOperators.name: SJVN Limited
hydroOperators.notes: Operates Nathpa Jhakri — largest hydro station in India. Expanding into solar, wind, thermal.

units.note: BHEL supplied Francis turbines. 27.5 km long headrace tunnel.

hydroOperators.name: NTPC Hydro / NTPC Renewable
hydroOperators.notes: NTPC operates Koldam (HP), Tapovan Vishnugad (UK) and Singrauli Small Hydro.

units.note: Damaged by 2021 Chamoli disaster. Restored 2023.

hydroOperators.name: THDC India Limited
hydroOperators.notes: Tehri Dam complex is India's tallest dam. Pumped storage project also under THDC.

units.note: Toshiba (Japan) supplied Francis turbines. India's tallest dam at 261 m.
Andritz (Austria) reversible pump-turbines. Largest pumped storage project in India. Key for grid balancing.

hydroOperators.name: Greenko Group (Hydro & PHES)
hydroOperators.notes: India's largest pumped hydro storage developer. QC Solar + hydro integrated RTC projects.

units.note: Andritz reversible pump-turbines. Integrated with 5.2 GWh storage for 24×7 green power.

hydroOperators.name: Kerala State Electricity Board (KSEB)
hydroOperators.notes: Kerala's hydro network — 55 hydroelectric projects feeding the state grid.

units.note: Highest arch dam in Asia at commissioning. Francis turbines supplied by BHEL.

hydroOperators.name: BBMB (Bhakra Beas Management Board)
hydroOperators.notes: Manages Bhakra-Nangal complex — India's oldest major hydroelectric system.

units.note: BHEL retrofitted original GE turbines in 1990s–2000s.
